subject: semfindr: Case influience on models fitted by lavaan

messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: semfindr: Case influience on models fitted by lavaan
parts:
Hi lavaan Google group members;

I would like to share a package Mark Lai and I developed, semfindr, "finder", without the "e":

https://sfcheung.github.io/semfindr/

The stable release is available on CRAN. The latest developmental release can be installed from GitHub:

remotes::install_github("sfcheung/semfindr")

It has one main goal:

- Help identifying influential cases, if any, in models fitted by lavaan (for now).

It can compute most of the measures introduced by Pek and MacCallum (2011) in their excellent paper on sensitivity analysis in SEM:

- several kinds of case influence measure on parameters.
- generalized Cook's distance on all free parameters or a subset of free paramters of interest (e.g., all path coefficients).
- case influence on fit measures, mainly model chi-square but any fit measures reported by lavaan::fitMeasures() are supported.
- Generating plots of case influence measures.

There are other packages for doing these tasks. However, we have projects with large samples and/or models difficult to fit (e.g., big models with missing data). We would like to have something more efficient to use in these projects. Hence this package, developed partly to meet our own needs but maybe it can also serve other researchers.

It supports two approaches:

- The conventional leave-one-out approach, but this phase only needs to be done once, and can be done on selected cases. The stored results can be reused by other case influence functions, such that case influence can be examined as often as desired without refitting the model for each case.

- An approximate approach (only for ML estimator) that approximtes some case influence measures without the need to refitting the model for each case. The measure is not exact, but usually close enough in ranking and can be computed quickly.

These two approaches can be used together. E.g.. use the approximate approach first to identify a potential set of influential cases quickly, and then use the leave-one-out approach to compute the exact influence.

More on the basic features can be found in the Get Started vignette:

https://sfcheung.github.io/semfindr/articles/semfindr.html

It still has some limitations. For example, it does not yet support multisample models. But this is our priority because we also have studies with multisample models.

Comments and bug reports are much appreciated. They would be great for helping us to improve the package.

Hope you find semfindr useful.

-- Shu Fai

Reference:

Pek, J., & MacCallum, R. (2011). Sensitivity analysis in structural equation models: Cases and their influence. Multivariate Behavioral Research, 46(2), 202-228. https://doi.org/10.1080/00273171.2011.561068
